spans.s: aśaikṣa, m. (= Pali asekha, asekkha; neg. of śaikṣa, q.v.), one who no longer needs religious training, being in the 8th stage (see Childers s.v. sekho); = arhant: ˚ṣaḥ Mvy 〔1734〕; ˚ṣa-mārgaḥ Mvy 〔1320〕, the third parivarta of the dharmacakra, in which ‘misery is known, its origin abandoned, its suppression attained, the way leading to its suppression realized’ (〔1321—24〕). Often in cpd. śaikṣāśaikṣa, or bracketed with śaikṣa as separate word; see śaikṣa; its place may be taken by arhant, e.g. Mv 〔i.158.7〕; Divy 〔399.24〕. Written aśaiṣya in LV 〔250.18〕, see s.v. śaiṣya.
